title: Ohio State approves $100 million settlement for victims in school doctor sexual abuse case
content:
Ohio State reached a $100 million settlement with hundreds of former student athletes who said university doctor Richard Strauss sexually abused them, allegations that first came from men’s wrestlers in 2018 and were followed by more claims from alumni of other teams.

The school previously reached six separate settlements totaling $61 million with 317 other victims.

During a board of trustees meeting Wednesday, school leaders approved a preliminary agreement with 279 of the 280 remaining victims of Strauss’ abuse involved in pending litigation.

“The survivors of the Strauss abuse are all Buckeyes, will always be a part of our family and our community, and I firmly believe that,” OSU president Ravi Bellamkonda said. “We continue to be very grateful to them for their courage in coming forward, and reaching a final resolution is very important to us and is an important step forward.”

Multiple athletes said they reported Strauss’ abuse to coaches or members of the athletic department, and the school failed to take action. Ohio State conducted an independent investigation after allegations were first raised and later issued a 182-page report in 2019 that confirmed Strauss abused at least 177 men and that multiple school officials and athletic department employees were aware of Strauss’ actions yet did not stop him.

Wednesday’s settlement, once finalized, is expected to largely end the legal battle between the school and the victims.

Former student athletes alleged that Strauss groped them, asked them to strip down unnecessarily during medical examinations, lingered in teams’ locker rooms and sometimes showered with teams.

Ohio State employed Strauss from 1978 to 1998, and he also ran an off-campus clinic. Strauss, who died by suicide in 2005, was never charged with a crime and denied the allegations.

In 2025, HBO released the documentary “Surviving Ohio State,” examining the culture that allowed Strauss’ abuse to continue for two decades. Chief among them was the imbalance of power between Strauss and his victims. Strauss controlled their medical clearance, which meant athletes had to see him to compete.

The film also focused on the victims’ coaches, investigating what they knew and how they responded. The biggest name publicly associated with this case is Jim Jordan, a former Ohio State assistant wrestling coach who is now a Republican congressman from Ohio.

At least seven victims, including some who hadn’t spoken publicly until appearing in the documentary, alleged Jordan knew of the abuse during his time at Ohio State. Jordan has repeatedly denied those allegations.

— Cameron Teague Robinson contributed to this report.
